benchmark_type_evidence: We introduce PolygloToxicityPrompts (PTP), the first large-scale multilingual toxicity evaluation benchmark of 425K naturally occurring prompts spanning 17 languages.
brief_description: A large-scale multilingual benchmark of 425K naturally occurring prompts across 17 languages for evaluating neural toxic degeneration in LLMs, created by scraping over 100M web-text documents from mC4 and The Pile corpora and scoring them with Perspective API. PTPSmall is a stratified 5K-per-language subset for lower-cost benchmarking.

datasets.translation_method: Approximately 83.2% naturally occurring (scraped from web-text). ~16.8% (~70K prompts across 9 languages) translated from toxic English/other-language samples using NLLB-3.3B model to supplement low-toxicity languages (ar, cs, fr, ko, id, it, nl, pl, sv).
datasets.annotation_method: Automated: documents scraped from mC4 and The Pile corpora (100M+ documents), scored for toxicity using Perspective API. Documents split in half to form prompts and continuations. 6250 documents sampled from each of 4 equal-width toxicity levels ([0, 0.25), [0.25, 0.5), [0.5, 0.75), [0.75, 1]) per language, yielding 25K prompts per language (425K total).

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Carnegie Mellon University, University of Virginia, Allen Institute for AI
data_creator_info.evidence: Dataset was created automatically by the research team via web scraping and automated toxicity scoring. No human annotators involved in dataset creation.

datasets.source_reference: mC4 (Xue et al., 2021) and The Pile (Gao et al., 2020) corpora; Pile Curse subset for English.
datasets.notes: Prompts are much longer than RealToxicityPrompts (~400 GPT-4 tokens average). For 9 languages with very low toxicity rates (<0.01% in mC4), synthetic high-toxicity data was added via machine translation.

datasets.variant_notes: A stratified sample of 5K prompts per language from the full PTP dataset, designed for benchmarking models with limited computational resources.
datasets.translation_method: Same as PTP (stratified subsample of PTP).
datasets.annotation_method: Stratified random sample from PTP; same toxicity scoring methodology via Perspective API.

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Carnegie Mellon University, University of Virginia, Allen Institute for AI

datasets.notes: 5K prompts per language (85K total). Used for the actual 62-model benchmarking due to computational constraints.

translated.evidence: Approximately 83.2% of the dataset is naturally occurring (scraped from web-text corpora). ~16.8% (~70K translated prompts across 9 languages: ar, cs, fr, ko, id, it, nl, pl, sv) were translated from toxic samples using the NLLB-3.3B model because these languages had <0.01% toxicity rates in the source corpora.

native_annotators.evidence: No human annotators were involved in dataset creation. The dataset was constructed entirely automatically via web scraping and Perspective API scoring.

culturally_grounded.evidence: The data is scraped from general web-text without cultural grounding design. It relies on Perspective API (a universal tool) rather than culturally-informed annotation. The paper acknowledges Perspective API has biases against some languages (e.g., German).

PolygloToxicityPrompts (PTP).annotation_quality_notes: Toxicity scores are generated automatically using Perspective API, an industry-standard but imperfect tool. The paper acknowledges: (1) toxicity is subjective, (2) Perspective API overestimates toxicity for text containing minority identity mentions, (3) it may be biased against certain languages like German. No human validation was performed.

translated.evidence: PTPSmall is a stratified subset of PTP, so it inherits the same mixed naturally-occurring/translated composition.

native_annotators.evidence: Same automated creation process as PTP—no human annotators.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Subset of PTP; same lack of cultural grounding design.

PTPSmall.annotation_quality_notes: Same as PTP—automated Perspective API scoring without human validation.

datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: The majority of PTP was scraped from naturally occurring web-text in each target language from mC4 and The Pile corpora, not translated from English. However, ~16.8% was machine-translated to augment high-toxicity data for low-toxicity languages.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: For 9 languages (ar, cs, fr, ko, id, it, nl, pl, sv) with very low toxicity rates in mC4, toxic samples were translated from English/other languages using NLLB-3.3B.

details.notes: PTP does not include culturally-grounded design. Although the authors argue naturally occurring web-text captures more authentic toxicity than translated benchmarks, there was no deliberate cultural adaptation or region-specific content creation.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: No human annotators were used in dataset creation. The entire pipeline is automated.

annotator_workforce.evidence: The dataset was created entirely through automated web scraping and Perspective API scoring by the research team. No human annotators were involved. The research was partly funded by Jigsaw.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is limited to 17 languages supported by Perspective API, all relatively high-resource. The authors acknowledge: 'our testbed does not extend to low-resource languages due to the lack of toxicity detection tools.' Perspective API is trained primarily on English data with known biases. The paper explicitly advocates for non-translated, naturally occurring data as superior to English-translated benchmarks.

sub_regions: Europe (Czech, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish)
notably_excluded: South/Southeast Asian languages beyond Hindi and Indonesian
geographic_representation.evidence: The 17 languages are constrained by Perspective API's language support. The paper acknowledges: 'our testbed does not extend to low-resource languages due to the lack of toxicity detection tools.'
